provenance.canonical-source: packages/core/src/tabs/{Tabs.tsx,Tabs.css,TabBar.tsx,TabBar.css,TabList.tsx,TabList.css,Tab.tsx,Tab.css,TabTrigger.tsx,TabTrigger.css,TabPanel.tsx,TabPanel.css,TabAction.tsx,index.ts} plus internal/{contexts/*,hooks/*,overflow/*,registry/useCollection.ts} for the behaviour contract and internal/overflow/TabOverflowList.{tsx,css} for the overflow part. site/docs/components/tabs/{index,accessibility}.mdx read for the documented keyboard contract and the component's own description; site/src/examples/tabs/{Appearance,ActiveColor,WithIcon,WithBadge,DisabledTabs,DividerAndInset,Overflow,AddANewTab,DismissibleTabs}.tsx read for defaults and composition.
provenance.core-tabs-not-lab-tabs: THERE IS NO `tabs-next` DIRECTORY IN THIS CLONE. The brief named one; a `find . -type d -name '*tabs-next*'` over the whole repo returns nothing. What exists is TWO tab implementations: packages/core/src/tabs (Tabs / TabBar / TabList / Tab / TabTrigger / TabPanel / TabAction) and packages/lab/src/tabs (Tabs / Tabstrip / Tab / TabPanel / TabActivationIndicator). THIS COLUMN TAKES CORE, for four independent reasons: (1) site/docs/components/tabs/index.mdx names the package as `@salt-ds/core` and points sourceCodeUrl at .../packages/core/src/tabs; (2) the core set is the compound/context API (Tabs+TabList+Tab+TabTrigger+TabPanel with a value-keyed registry) that the -next generation introduced, i.e. it IS the graduated tabs-next; (3) the lab set is the legacy Tabstrip API with its own useTabstrip/useKeyboardNavigation/useSelection/drag-drop layer and an editable-label dependency, none of which the docs surface; (4) the two disagree structurally, most visibly on the indicator — lab has a MEASURED SLIDING thumb (TabActivationIndicator + useActivationIndicator, `transition: left 0.3s ease`, a getBoundingClientRect diff against the strip and a 50ms setTimeout to survive overflow restores) while core draws a STATIC per-tab ::after with no transition anywhere. Taking lab would have made Salt's cell for structure.indicator-motion `slide` instead of `static` — the single biggest cell in this matrix — so the choice is recorded rather than assumed.
provenance.accent-pin: --salt-navigable-accent-indicator-active and --salt-selectable-borderColor-selected both resolve through palette-accent, which carries a data-accent axis (blue default, teal alternate; next/palette/accent.css). This column pins BLUE, matching button/input/select/dialog.salt.json; only calendar.salt.json models byAccent. Recorded, not modelled.
provenance.surface-primary / -secondary / -tertiary: TabList.css .saltTabList-activeColor{Primary,Secondary,Tertiary} { --saltTabList-activeColor: var(--salt-container-{primary,secondary,tertiary}-background) } -> next/characteristics/container.css -> palette-background-{primary,secondary,tertiary} -> next/palette/background.css: snow rgb(255,255,255) / marble rgb(245,247,248) / limestone rgb(250,248,242) light, jet rgb(16,24,32) / granite rgb(26,34,41) / leather rgb(38,41,43) dark (next/foundations/color.css *-rgb triples).
provenance.active-color: THE SOURCE'S OWN INDIRECTION, reproduced rather than expanded. Salt does not write three background rules; it writes one rule reading --saltTabList-activeColor and three one-line classes that reassign it. Exactly one consumer: `.saltTabList-bordered .saltTab.saltTab-selected { background: var(--saltTabList-activeColor) }`. Its default here is var(--surface-primary), matching activeColor='primary'.
provenance.fg / fg-disabled: Tab.css color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground) and .saltTab-disabled color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground-disabled) -> next/characteristics/content.css -> palette-foreground-primary(-disabled) -> next/palette/foreground.css -> color-black / color-black-40a light, color-white / color-white-40a dark. NOTE the resting colour is FULL-STRENGTH: Salt does not de-emphasise an unselected tab the way shadcn (60%) and M3 (on-surface-variant) do.
provenance.divider: TabBar.css .saltTabBar-divider::before border-bottom and Tab.css's selected left/right borders are BOTH var(--salt-separable-secondary-borderColor) -> next/characteristics/separable.css -> palette-alpha-contrast-medium -> next/palette/alpha.css black-30a light / white-30a dark. NOTE this is the SECONDARY separable stop (30%), a step stronger than the tertiary (20%) Salt's dialog border and select group divider use. One token, three consumers here (bar divider, selected tab's left border, selected tab's right border).
provenance.indicator-hover: Tab.css `.saltTab:hover::after, .saltTab-focusVisible::after { background: var(--salt-navigable-indicator-hover) }` -> next/characteristics/navigable.css -> --salt-palette-neutral -> next/palette/neutral.css -> color-gray-500 = rgb(114,119,125), IDENTICAL in the light and dark blocks, hence modeInvariant. This grey preview of the active mark is unique to Salt among the three.
provenance.indicator-active: Tab.css `.saltTab.saltTab-selected::after { background: var(--salt-navigable-accent-indicator-active) }` -> navigable.css -> --salt-palette-accent -> blue-500 rgb(0,120,207), identical in both mode blocks.
provenance.accent / accent-weakest: TabOverflowList.css border: ... var(--salt-selectable-borderColor-selected) -> next/characteristics/selectable.css -> palette-accent (blue-500, mode-invariant) — the overflow list is framed in BLUE, the same finding SELECT-MATRIX.md finding 5 recorded for OptionList. The item hover is --salt-selectable-background-hover -> palette-accent-weakest -> blue-100 rgb(234,246,255) light / blue-900 rgb(0,23,54) dark. Values reused verbatim from select.salt.json rather than re-derived.
provenance.focus-outline: Tab.css `.saltTab-focusVisible { outline: var(--salt-focused-outline) }` and TabPanel.css `:focus-visible { outline: var(--salt-focused-outline) }` -> next/characteristics/focused.css: --salt-focused-outlineWidth (size-fixed-200 = 2px, density-invariant) --salt-focused-outlineStyle (borderStyle-dotted) --salt-focused-outlineColor (palette-accent-stronger) -> next/palette/accent.css: blue-700 rgb(0,69,126) light / blue-300 rgb(154,189,245) dark. Carried as one shorthand slot because the width and style are mode-invariant and only the colour moves.
provenance.popup-shadow: TabOverflowList.css box-shadow: var(--salt-overlayable-shadow-popout) -> next/characteristics/overlayable.css -> --salt-shadow-mediumLow. Value reused from docs/foundations/elevation.md (0 6px 10px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2) light / 0.55 dark), the same reuse tooltip.salt.json and select.salt.json made.
provenance.byDensity.tab-min-height / popup-max-hei: Tab.css AND TabList.css both declare min-height: calc(var(--salt-size-base) + var(--salt-spacing-100)) -> size-base 20/28/36/44 (foundations/size.css) + spacing-100 4/8/12/16 (foundations/spacing.css) = 24/36/48/60px. The overflow list's max-height is the five-row multiple of the same expression, from the size() middleware's `max(calc((var(--salt-size-base) + var(--salt-spacing-100)) * 5), calc(availableHeight - spacing-100))` — only the five-row floor is expressible without a positioning engine, exactly the partial select.salt.json declared for its option list.
provenance.byDensity.tab-padding: Tab.css padding: var(--salt-spacing-50) var(--salt-spacing-100). spacing-50 = 0.5 x spacing-100 = 2/4/6/8; spacing-100 = 4/8/12/16.
provenance.byDensity.tab-gap / list-gap: Tab.css gap AND TabTrigger.css gap AND TabList.css gap AND TabBar.css .saltTabBar-strip gap are ALL var(--salt-spacing-100) = 4/8/12/16px. One token, four declarations.
provenance.byDensity.indicator-height: Tab.css `.saltTab::after { height: var(--salt-size-indicator) }` -> foundations/size.css 2/3/4/5px. FROZEN-TOKEN CHECK: size-indicator is on the DENSITY scale, not the fixed scale, so it genuinely moves; snapshotting the medium 3px would have been wrong at three of four densities. Its siblings in the same rule — left/right: calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -1) — ARE on the fixed scale (1px, density-invariant by design, docs/foundations/sizes.md), so that -1px literal is correct everywhere.
provenance.byDensity.icon-size: NOT DECLARED IN Tab.css AT ALL. A tab icon is an ordinary @salt-ds/icons glyph and its box comes from packages/icons/src/icon/Icon.css: `--icon-size: max(calc(var(--salt-size-icon) * 1), 12px)`. size-icon is 10/12/14/16, so the rendered value is 12/12/14/16 — the high-density value is CLAMPED by Salt's own documented 12px readability floor, not frozen. Re-verified here rather than copied from SELECT-MATRIX.md finding 9's identical result for the chevron.
provenance.byDensity.type-tab: Tab.css declares the ramp property by property: font-family var(--salt-text-fontFamily) (typography-fontFamily-openSans), font-weight var(--salt-text-fontWeight) (typography-fontWeight-regular = 400), font-size/line-height var(--salt-text-fontSize)/var(--salt-text-lineHeight) -> next/characteristics/text.css density blocks 11/14 - 12/16 - 14/18 - 16/20, plus letter-spacing var(--salt-text-letterSpacing) = 0 and text-align var(--salt-text-textAlign) = left. SALT IS THE ONLY SYSTEM OF THE THREE THAT LEAVES ITS TAB LABEL AT REGULAR WEIGHT — shadcn uses font-medium and M3 uses title-small, both 500.
provenance.byDensity.popup-shape / popup-gap / over: TabOverflowList.css border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner, 0) -> next/palette/corner.css [data-corner=rounded] -> curve-150 -> foundations/curve.css 3/6/9/12px (the same unsuffixed stop Salt's dialog panel and select popup use); .saltTabOverflowList-listContainer gap: var(--salt-spacing-fixed-100) = 1px, density-invariant by design; the item's padding-left/right: var(--salt-spacing-100) = 4/8/12/16 with no vertical padding at all (the min-height does the work).
provenance.no-transition: CONFIRMED ABSENCE across the whole component: `grep -n 'transition\|animation' packages/core/src/tabs/*.css` returns nothing in Tabs.css, TabBar.css, TabList.css, Tab.css, TabTrigger.css or TabPanel.css. A Salt tab's indicator, background and border all change instantly. This is the direct reason structure.indicator-motion is `static` here and `fade` for shadcn.
provenance.no-selected-label-change: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: `.saltTab.saltTab-selected` and `.saltTabList-bordered .saltTab.saltTab-selected` between them set background, border-left, border-right and the ::after background. Neither touches `color` and neither touches `font-weight`. A selected Salt tab's TEXT is byte-identical to an unselected one's — which is why style.tab.color@selected is off in this column and on in the other two.
provenance.dead-alignment-css: RECORDED, NOT MODELLED: TabList.css defines `.saltTabList-center { justify-content: center }` and `.saltTabList-right { justify-content: flex-end }`, but TabList.tsx composes only withBaseName(), withBaseName(appearance), withBaseName('horizontal') and withBaseName(`activeColor${...}`) — there is no `align` prop and nothing applies either class. Dead CSS in this revision. No prop row was invented for it.
provenance.horizontal-only: TabList.tsx hard-codes withBaseName('horizontal') and TabList.css contains no `.saltTabList-horizontal` rule and no vertical counterpart. Salt tabs are horizontal-only; the ONLY vertical tablist in the component is the overflow popup's inner div (role=tablist aria-orientation=vertical), which is a different element with different keys.
provenance.overflow-declared-gap: TabOverflowList.tsx composes @floating-ui/react (offset(1), size() writing maxHeight inline, flip(), shift({padding:8})), useClick + useDismiss, a FloatingComponent with focusManagerProps {initialFocus: 0, returnFocus: false, modal: false, closeOnFocusOut: true}, a ResizeObserver that closes the menu on any strip resize, and a portal render mode that MOVES each tab's display:contents host element between measure/main/overflow slots rather than re-rendering it. The skeleton reproduces the observable contract only — see the template's behavior.overflow-navigation note. Style cells cover the list box, the restyled item and its hover; the positioning engine is a DECLARED GAP.
provenance.tab-action-composition: TabAction.tsx renders <Button appearance="transparent" sentiment="neutral"> with tabIndex={focused || selected ? undefined : -1}, an aria-labelledby chaining the tab id and its own, and a registerAction callback so TabTrigger can publish aria-actions (feature-detected) and an aria-description of '<n> actions available'. Every visual property belongs to the composed Button. DECLARED COMPOSITION; no style cell is modelled and the skeleton renders a neutral placeholder.

structure.tab-bar.source: TabBar.tsx — a separate exported component rendering .saltTabBar wrapping .saltTabBar-strip, with divider and inset boolean props

structure.tab-shell.source: Tab.tsx renders a role="presentation" div carrying every box style; TabTrigger.tsx renders the role="tab" button inside it with `all: unset` and a ::before full-size hit area

structure.indicator-motion.source: Tab.css's ::after is a per-tab pseudo-element with NO transition or animation rule anywhere in the component's CSS — the mark appears and disappears instantly. (The legacy packages/lab/src/tabs implementation DOES slide, via TabActivationIndicator's `transition: left 0.3s ease`; that is the other implementation, see the core-tabs-not-lab-tabs note.)

structure.tab-badge.source: site/src/examples/tabs/WithBadge.tsx composes <Badge value={n} aria-hidden/> inside the TabTrigger; DECLARED COMPOSITION to the future badge component

behavior.roving-tabindex.source: TabTrigger.tsx: isTabStop = !hidden && (focused || selected || active || fallbackTabStop), where fallbackTabStop = !hasSelectedTab && location === 'main' && order === 0

behavior.arrow-keys.source: TabList.tsx handleKeyDown actionMap = { ArrowRight: getNext, ArrowLeft: getPrevious, Home: getFirst, End: getLast } — no Up/Down branch on the strip. accessibility.mdx: 'Left arrow / Right arrow — moves focus between tab items in tab bar'; 'Up arrow / Down arrow — moves focus between tab items in an overflow menu list'.

behavior.home-end.source: TabList.tsx actionMap Home/End; documented in accessibility.mdx

behavior.wrap.source: Tabs.tsx useCollection({ targetWindow, wrap: true }); getNext does (index + 1) % items.length, getPrevious does (index - 1 + len) % len

behavior.activation-mode.source: MANUAL, and it is explicit on both sides. TabList's arrow handler only calls nextItem.element?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); TabTrigger's handleFocus records activeTab and scrolls, and does NOT call setSelected. Selection happens in handleClick and in handleKeyDown's `if (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ')` branch. accessibility.mdx: 'Enter / Space — selects a tab item'.

behavior.disabled-navigation.source: Tab.tsx sets aria-disabled, NOT the native disabled attribute; TabTrigger's tabIndex rule never consults `disabled`; and internal/registry/useCollection.ts's getNavigableItems filters only on `item.location === 'hidden'` and `!!item.element`. So arrow keys land on a disabled Salt tab. Activation is blocked separately: onClick is undefined when disabled, and handleKeyDown preventDefaults Enter/Space and returns.

behavior.pointer-activation.source: TabTrigger.tsx handleClick -> setSelected(event, value, selectionSource), bound as onClick. onMouseDown exists on Tab.tsx but only records activeTab and the wasMouseDown flag that suppresses the focus ring.

behavior.panel-focusable.source: TabPanel.tsx tabIndex={hidden || hasFocusableChildren ? undefined : 0}, where hasFocusableChildren comes from tabbable(element).length > 0 re-run behind a rAF-debounced MutationObserver on childList/subtree/attributes

behavior.panel-mounting.source: TabPanel.tsx always renders and sets hidden={hidden || undefined}; TabPanel.css .saltTabPanel[hidden] { display: none }

behavior.scroll-into-view.source: TabTrigger.tsx handleFocus: event.currentTarget.parentElement?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' }) — the PARENT (the Tab div), with the source comment 'Ensures the associated tab is in view.'; TabList focuses with preventScroll: true so this is the only scroller

behavior.overflow-navigation.source: TabOverflowList.tsx (floating-ui popup, ResizeObserver auto-close, Shift+Tab return-to-button) + TabTrigger.tsx's location === 'overflow' branch handling ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End through tabListLayout.moveOverflowFocus

prop.appearance.source: TabListProps.appearance?: 'bordered' | 'transparent', DEFAULT 'bordered' -> contained. Listed default-first per the select.shadcn.json convention: the skeleton and the harness both take value[0] as the resting state.

prop.emphasis.note: no equivalent axis — Salt's two-way axis is appearance (contained/plain), already modelled

prop.orientation.source: TabList.tsx hard-codes withBaseName('horizontal'); there is no orientation prop and TabList.css has no vertical rule. See the horizontal-only provenance note.

prop.divider.source: TabBarProps.divider?: boolean — 'Styling variant with a bottom separator. Defaults to false'. Note every site example nevertheless passes it.

prop.inset.source: TabBarProps.inset?: boolean — 'Styling variant with left and right padding. Defaults to false'

prop.disabled.source: TabProps.disabled?: boolean — 'If true, the tab will be disabled'; rendered as aria-disabled on the trigger and a .saltTab-disabled class on the shell

state.hover.source: Tab.css .saltTab:hover::after — the INDICATOR, not the label

state.disabled.source: Tab.css .saltTab.saltTab-disabled plus the explicit .saltTab-disabled:hover::after { background: none } cancellation

state.pressed.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE on the strip — Tab.css has no :active rule. The only :active styling in the whole component is TabOverflowList.css's `.saltTabOverflowList-list .saltTab:active`, which belongs to the overflow menu.

state.overflowing.source: TabList.tsx data-ismeasuring + Tab.css's @supports-guarded `.saltTabList:has([data-overflowbutton]) .saltTab { max-width: calc(100% - var(--salt-spacing-100) - var(--salt-size-base)) }`

style.tab-bar.divider.source: TabBar.css .saltTabBar-divider::before { inset: auto 0 0 0; height: var(--salt-size-fixed-100); border-bottom: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) var(--salt-separable-secondary-borderColor) }. size-fixed-100 = 1px on the FIXED scale, density-invariant by design. Reproduced as a border on the bar itself rather than a pseudo-element, since the pseudo carries no other property.

style.tablist.background.source: TabList.css `background: transparent` — DECLARED, not merely absent

style.tablist.background@plain.note: the strip is transparent in both appearances; nothing changes

style.tablist.color.note: Salt declares colour on the tab (Tab.css), not the list

style.tablist.min-height.source: TabList.css min-height: calc(var(--salt-size-base) + var(--salt-spacing-100)) — the identical expression Tab.css uses, so the tab exactly fills the strip

style.tablist.gap@plain.note: the gap does not change with appearance

style.tablist.padding.note: no padding on .saltTabList; horizontal insets belong to the BAR (style.tab-bar.inset)

style.tablist.shape.note: no border-radius in TabList.css — a Salt tab strip is square

style.tablist.orientation@vertical.note: horizontal-only; see the horizontal-only provenance note

style.tab.color.source: Tab.css color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground) — full strength, no de-emphasis

style.tab.min-width.source: Tab.css min-width: 4em — a bare em literal with no override variable, the same floor Dropdown.css declares. Em-relative, so it tracks the density-driven font size rather than freezing it.

style.tab.flex.note: Salt tabs are content-sized and flex-shrink: 0; only the TabTrigger inside is flex: 1, which is in the template's base

style.tab.gap.source: declared on BOTH .saltTab and .saltTabTrigger in source — one token, two declarations, which the row's doubled selector reproduces

style.tab.border.source: Tab.css border: none; border-left/border-right: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) var(--salt-borderStyle-solid) transparent. Only the SIDES are reserved, because only the sides gain a colour when the tab is selected under the bordered appearance.

style.tab.overflow.source: Tab.css overflow: hidden — which clips the ::after's own left/right -1px extension back off. Reproduced as source has it.

style.tab.transition.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no transition or animation rule in any of the six CSS files

style.tab.color@hover.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Tab.css's only :hover rule targets ::after. A hovered Salt tab's label does not change.

style.tab.color@selected.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — see the no-selected-label-change provenance note. Neither colour nor weight moves.

style.tab.selected-fill@contained.source: Tab.css `.saltTabList-bordered .saltTab.saltTab-selected { background: var(--saltTabList-activeColor); border-left: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) solid var(--salt-separable-secondary-borderColor); border-right: ... }`. Modelled as a colour reassignment on the reserved transparent borders so the box does not shift.

style.tab.state-layer@hover.note: no state-layer mechanism in Salt; the hover feedback is the indicator preview

style.tab.focus.source: Tab.css .saltTab-focusVisible { outline: var(--salt-focused-outline) } — on the TAB DIV, with TabTrigger.css's `:focus-visible { outline: none }` suppressing the button's own so the ring is drawn once

style.tab.disabled.source: Tab.css .saltTab.saltTab-disabled { cursor: var(--salt-cursor-disabled); color: var(--salt-content-primary-foreground-disabled) }. NOTE no pointer-events: none — a disabled Salt tab is still hoverable and still arrow-reachable.

style.indicator.edge.source: Tab.css .saltTab::after { left: calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -1); right: calc(var(--salt-size-fixed-100) * -1) } plus `.saltTabList-transparent .saltTab::after { bottom: 0 }`. size-fixed-100 is 1px on the fixed scale, density-invariant, so the literal is correct at every density.

style.indicator.edge@contained.source: Tab.css `.saltTabList-bordered .saltTab::after { top: 0 }` — Salt's DEFAULT appearance marks the TOP edge, not the bottom

style.indicator.shape.note: no border-radius on the ::after — a square mark

style.indicator.rest.source: Tab.css's ::after declares content/position/left/right/height and NO background; the fill arrives only from the hover, focus-visible and selected rules

style.indicator.background@focus-visible.source: Tab.css .saltTab-focusVisible::after — the same rule, the same value; with manual activation this preview is the whole visual feedback of arrowing

style.indicator.selected@contained.note: Salt's contained appearance SHOWS its mark (moved to the top edge); only shadcn hides it

style.tab-icon.size.source: packages/icons/src/icon/Icon.css --icon-size: max(calc(var(--salt-size-icon) * 1), 12px) -> 12/12/14/16px. NOT declared in Tab.css; the 12px is a live floor, not a snapshot.

style.tab-icon.color.note: no .saltIcon-primary/-secondary class is applied inside a tab, so the glyph is currentColor and inherits the tab's colour including the disabled 40% alpha

style.panel.outline.note: Salt does the opposite of suppressing it — see style.panel.focus

style.overflow-list.box.source: TabOverflowList.css .saltTabOverflowList-list { background: var(--salt-container-primary-background); border: var(--salt-size-fixed-100) solid var(--salt-selectable-borderColor-selected); border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner, 0); box-shadow: var(--salt-overlayable-shadow-popout); z-index: var(--salt-zIndex-flyover) } + .saltTabOverflowList-listContainer { gap: var(--salt-spacing-fixed-100) } + the size() middleware's five-row max-height floor. zIndex-flyover = 1500 (foundations/zindex.css, docs/foundations/layers.md).

style.overflow-item.box.source: TabOverflowList.css `.saltTabOverflowList-list .saltTab` re-declares background var(--salt-selectable-background) (color-transparent), min-height calc(size-base + spacing-100), padding-left/right var(--salt-spacing-100), justify-content: flex-start, and `::after { display: none }` — the indicator is switched off inside the menu (reproduced in the template's base). The min-width override `max-width: unset` under the :has() guard is the same rule from the other direction.
